subject: creating mirror reflection of one-side landmarks

messages.author: 8bcb7cabc778c7da
messages.subject: creating mirror reflection of one-side landmarks
parts:
Dear Geomorphers,

I'm working with a 2D landmark data set of vertebrae in anterior view in which one side (right) has been landmarked, with 5 landmarks along the midplane axis for a total of 12 landmarks. 

I would like to generate a mirror reflection of the paired landmarks, and wonder if there is an easy way to do this in geomorph or another program. I naively tried multiplying the x coordinate dimensions *-1 and keeping y the same, but since the midplane x coordinates are not at 0 this obviously doesn't work.

Any advice or code would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks,
Christy

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] creating mirror reflection of one-side landmarks
parts:
Hi Christy,

I do not know that there is any standard routine to do that, but it should be fairly easy to write one in R. I guess one would need to find the actual reflection plane through e.g. an RMA regression of the points of the midline, set that as x = 0 and then mirror the coordinates as you were doing.

Hope this helps

Antigoni

In Claude's book [Claude - Morphometrics With R - 2008] you can find some script on which to base yourself upon to make the mirror reflection.

You should be able to find the .pdf online.



Best wishes,
